drills.q: Assign table plans: request telemetry, verbose debug traces, 7-year audit events, security logs.
drills.a: Requests -> Analytics (joins, included queries, 31d). Debug traces -> Basic (cheap ingest, single-table scans OK). Audit -> Auxiliary + LTR years (search jobs on demand). Security -> Analytics if Sentinel (90d incl., alerting needs) + LTR beyond.

drills.q: Observability bill 5x after container migration. First suspect?
drills.a: Console logging provider left enabled in production - documented case cut ~87% of observability cost just disabling it; also filter health-check endpoints in DCR transformations.

drills.q: Error logs missing during outage investigation. What happened and fix?
drills.a: Daily cap hit - ingestion silently stopped. Alert on cap-near metrics; caps are emergency brakes only; real control = transformations, plan routing, sampling upstream.

drills.q: Dashboards fine but users report slowness. Sampling connection?
drills.a: Adaptive sampling thinned the slow-tail individual traces while pre-sample metrics stayed accurate; keep metrics for truth, add full-fidelity capture on error paths, surface trace-ids to clients for targeted hunting.

drills.q: One log alert fired 400 times in minutes during a blip. Redesign.
drills.a: Match evaluation frequency to remediation cadence, add suppression via alert-processing rules, migrate volume conditions to metric alerts (possibly custom metrics via summary rules); log alerts reserved for semantic cross-resource conditions.

drills.q: Finance can't reconcile invoice to teams. Two fixes.
drills.a: Use amortized views so reservations/savings plans spread correctly, and enforce tag governance via Policy deny-on-missing + inherit-from-RG with compliance dashboards from Resource Graph queries.

drills.q: KQL over billions of rows takes minutes. Optimization sequence?
drills.a: TimeGenerated filter first, project columns early, summarize before joins, has > contains, summary-rule aggregates for dashboards; structural answer: move that workload's raw data to cheaper plans and query summaries.

drills.q: Budget alerted, nobody acted, bill doubled. What failed?
drills.a: Operating model: budgets notify but never enforce; budget events must route into owner-tagged actionable workflows with escalation runbooks; actual guardrails live in Policy (allowed SKUs, tag requirements, region constraints).

drills.q: Synthetic availability tests pass but users broken. Why layer RUM?
drills.a: Synthetics test happy-path reachability from Azure POPs, not user reality (third-party scripts, ISP issues, client rendering); OTel browser SDK real-user telemetry beneath synthetics; alert on divergence between the two.

drills.q: Rank ops failure frequency: ingestion cost creep, sampling-blind forensics, alert fatigue misses, cap-induced evidence loss.
drills.a: 1 cost creep (every new service adds silently), 2 alert fatigue (accumulates until real page drowns), 3 sampling-blind forensics (bites when debugging outliers), 4 cap evidence loss (rarest, most catastrophic per event).

drills.q: Explain why Application Insights' shift to OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation matters architecturally.
drills.a: It replaces the older proprietary Application Insights SDK with the same vendor-neutral instrumentation standard AWS (X-Ray) and GCP (Cloud Trace) have adopted, closing a real portability gap -- instrumentation code becomes more reusable across backends rather than locking an application into Azure-specific tracing APIs.
